dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: yatra yatra manas tuṣṭir manas tatraiva dhārayet | tatra tatra parānandasvarūpaṃ sampravartate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 74: GRETIL reads -svārūpaṃ; corrected to -svarūpaṃ with Wallis and Pradīpaka.
dharana.rendering: Wherever the mind finds contentment, let it be held right there; in each such place the very nature of supreme bliss shows itself.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: tuṣṭi means a deep, moving delight, not agitation: one in which everything external is forgotten, thought-constructs fall away and the mind is unruffled. One should plunge into the source of that delight and find it to be the divine, the Self of all.
dharana.technique_name: Resting the Mind Wherever It Is Content
dharana.instruction: Whenever you notice the mind is quietly content, stay right there and rest in it.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 74 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: any place, activity or object where the mind is quietly content
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map can be anywhere: whatever place or moment in the day brings quiet contentment, attention settles there.
geometry.svg_hint: a scatter of small soft points across a day-line, each glowing gently
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Settle where it is good
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a restless mind stops seeking and settles where it is already content. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Notice where the mind is already content, and stay there
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes open; this happens in ordinary life
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Any moment of quiet contentment, held without reaching for more

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Wherever the mind finds contentment, let it be held right there; in each such place the very nature of supreme bliss shows itself.
adiyogi.method_summary: During the day, notice when the mind is quietly content (a cup of tea, a view, a task going well). Instead of moving on, hold the mind right there and rest in the contentment itself.

honesty.disclosure: Door 051 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 51 (verse 74) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 051 is dharana 51, verse 74. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Choose quiet, harmless contentment, not agitation or compulsion. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Attention
